abstract: The paper investigates LSTM networks for keystroke biometric authentication in free-text scenarios, achieving 2.2% and 9.2% EER for physical and touchscreen keyboards. It compares multiple loss functions, datasets, and architectures, demonstrating scalability to 100,000 users with state-of-the-art performance.

research.problem: Scalable keystroke biometric authentication in free-text scenarios with high intra-class variability.
research.motivation: Ubiquitous keyboard usage and growing security threats necessitate robust, large-scale biometric authentication solutions.
research.objective: Evaluate deep learning architectures for scaling free-text keystroke biometrics to hundreds of thousands of users.

methodology.summary: LSTM-based TypeNet models trained with diverse loss functions (softmax, contrastive, triplet) and evaluated across four datasets with varying device types and sequence lengths.
methodology.training_strategy: Varying sample sizes and sequence lengths across device types

experiments.experimental_setup: Evaluated EER across 100-100,000 test subjects for desktop and mobile scenarios, with 30,000 subjects for touchscreen keyboards.
experiments.results: TypeNet achieved 2.2% EER (physical keyboards) and 9.2% EER (touchscreen keyboards), outperforming prior approaches by >50%.

contributions: First large-scale free-text keystroke biometrics system with 136M keystrokes
State-of-the-art EER reduction via triplet loss optimization
limitations: Requires extensive keystroke data for enrollment
Performance degrades with extremely short sequences
analysis.research_gap: Prior systems lacked scalability to massive user bases and diverse device environments.

sections.introduction: Introduces keystroke dynamics as a behavioral biometric, emphasizing its role in internet authentication and security challenges.
sections.related_work: Reviews prior approaches including statistical models, HMMs, and early deep learning methods for keystroke biometrics.
sections.methodology: Details LSTM architecture, loss function variations, and cross-device dataset analysis for scalability evaluation.
sections.results: Reports EER benchmarks across 100K+ users and comparative performance against existing methods.
sections.discussion: Analyzes scalability factors and trade-offs between different loss functions and dataset configurations.
sections.conclusion: Summarizes TypeNet's scalability achievements and potential for large-scale internet authentication systems.

metadata.title: Covert lie detection using keyboard dynamics

abstract: The paper presents a method for covert lie detection using keystroke dynamics to distinguish liars from truth-tellers with 95% accuracy. Unexpected questions are used to reveal deception clues through analysis of typing patterns, offering an alternative to traditional biometric verification methods.

research.problem: Identifying fake identities without external verification criteria (e.g., documents, biometrics).
research.motivation: Threats from false identities in terrorism and online services require improved deception detection methods.
research.objective: Develop a covert lie detection system using keystroke dynamics to identify deception in identity verification.
research_questions: Can keystroke dynamics distinguish liars from truth-tellers?
How do unexpected questions affect deception detection through typing patterns?

methodology.summary: Keystroke dynamics analysis combined with machine learning models to classify responses based on typing patterns during identity verification tasks.
models: Classification models for truth-teller vs. liar detection
datasets: 60 participants (40 training, 20 testing) with personal information-based questions
preprocessing: GULPEASE readability index adjustment for reaction time
methodology.training_strategy: Supervised machine learning using labeled training data from truthful and deceptive responses.

experiments.experimental_setup: Participants answered 18 questions (control, expected, unexpected) about personal identity. Keystroke data was recorded via an online interface with PHP/HTML/JavaScript.
baselines: Traditional biometric verification methods (fingerprints, retina scans)
experiments.results: Keystroke analysis achieved 95% accuracy in distinguishing liars from truth-tellers using unexpected questions.

contributions: Novel covert lie detection method using keystroke dynamics
Framework for online identity verification without explicit yes/no prompts
advantages: Operational in online contexts (e.g., subscription forms)
No need for pre-recorded typing patterns
limitations: Requires predefined questions for deception detection
Dependent on question complexity and cognitive load
future_work: Real-time deception detection in dynamic environments
analysis.research_gap: Limited studies on keystroke dynamics for identity deception detection compared to mouse tracking methods.

sections.introduction: Addresses the challenge of verifying identities without physical evidence, proposing keystroke dynamics as a covert deception detection method.
sections.related_work: Reviews existing biometric verification systems and prior work on mouse dynamics for lie detection.
sections.methodology: Details the experimental design, question types, and keystroke feature extraction process.
sections.results: Reports 95% accuracy in distinguishing liars from truth-tellers using unexpected questions and keystroke analysis.
sections.discussion: Analyzes cognitive mechanisms of deception and the advantages of keystroke dynamics over traditional methods.
sections.conclusion: Demonstrates the effectiveness of covert keystroke analysis for identity verification, highlighting its potential in security applications.

metadata.title: Non-Acted Text and Keystrokes Database and Learning Methods to Recognize Emotions
metadata.venue: ACM Trans. Multimedia Comput. Commun. Appl.

abstract: This work presents a multimodal text-keystrokes dataset and associated learning methods for emotion recognition. A dataset of 69 participants' text and keystroke data is collected, achieving 86.95% accuracy through feature fusion and outperforming state-of-the-art techniques in accuracy.

research.problem: Identifying dominant emotions from limited text data for human-computer interaction.
research.motivation: Enhance emotion recognition in computing systems using non-acted text and keystroke dynamics.
research.objective: Create a multimodal dataset and learning methods for accurate emotion detection from short text and keystrokes.

methodology.summary: Combines text and keystroke features from 69 participants' data using supervised learning and feature selection techniques.
methodology.training_strategy: Supervised learning with feature selection methods

experiments.experimental_setup: Data collected from 69 participants in controlled environments with video stimuli and unguided text reviews.
experiments.results: 86.95% accuracy via text-keystroke fusion; 100% accuracy for pleasure-displeasure classes using SVM with feature fusion.

contributions: Novel multimodal dataset combining text and keystrokes
Balanced labeled dataset for five basic emotions
limitations: Reliance on text and keystroke data
future_work: Expanding to other modalities like speech or EEG
analysis.research_gap: Lack of publicly available labeled datasets with comprehensive emotion classes.

sections.introduction: Discusses challenges in emotion recognition and motivation for multimodal data collection.
sections.related_work: References prior studies on affective computing and emotion detection methods.
sections.methodology: Details dataset collection, feature extraction, and learning framework design.
sections.results: Presents accuracy metrics and comparison with state-of-the-art techniques.
sections.discussion: Analyzes contributions, advantages, and limitations of the proposed approach.
sections.conclusion: Summarizes the work's impact on emotion recognition and future directions.

metadata.title: The Influence of Emotion on Keyboard Typing: An Experimental Study Using Auditory Stimuli

abstract: This study investigates how emotions influence keyboard typing patterns using auditory stimuli. Keystroke dynamics were analyzed through a controlled experiment with International Affective Digitized Sounds (IADS), revealing significant effects of arousal on keystroke duration and latency, but not accuracy. The findings suggest potential for improving emotion recognition technology through personalized models.

research.problem: Limited investigation into emotion-induced variance in keyboard typing patterns.
research.motivation: Keystroke dynamics offer non-intrusive, easily obtainable data for emotion recognition.
research.objective: Examine variance sources in typing patterns caused by emotions using controlled experiments.
research_questions: Do keystroke features exceed significance levels under different emotional states?
How large are emotional contributions to keystroke feature variances?

methodology.summary: Two-way ANOVA analyzed keystroke duration, latency, and accuracy using IADS stimuli. Keystroke dynamics were recorded during typing tasks with standardized equipment.
methodology.training_strategy: Traditional statistical methods without complex ML algorithms.

experiments.experimental_setup: Subjects typed '748596132' after IADS-2 sounds, with SAM ratings for valence and arousal. 63 trials with 3 practice sessions.
experiments.results: Arousal significantly affected duration (p < .05) and latency (p < .01), but not accuracy. Emotional effects were smaller than individual variability.

contributions: Supports arousal's impact on keystroke dynamics
Highlights potential for personalized emotion recognition models
limitations: Small emotional effect size relative to individual variability
future_work: Longitudinal studies on emotional state impacts
analysis.research_gap: Need for deeper exploration of emotional state-keystroke dynamics relationships.

sections.introduction: Discusses context-aware computing and emotion recognition challenges, emphasizing keystroke dynamics as a non-intrusive approach.
sections.related_work: Reviews existing emotion recognition methods (facial expressions, speech, physiology) and keystroke dynamics research gaps.
sections.methodology: Describes experimental design, IADS-2 stimuli, SAM ratings, and statistical analysis framework.
sections.results: Reports arousal's significant effects on duration and latency, with limited impact on accuracy.
sections.discussion: Analyzes implications for emotion recognition technology and limitations of current approaches.
sections.conclusion: Summarizes findings on arousal's influence on keystroke dynamics and suggests future research directions.

metadata.title: DeepMood: Modeling Mobile Phone Typing Dynamics for Mood Detection

abstract: The paper explores using mobile phone typing metadata to detect mood disturbances. It proposes DeepMood, an end-to-end deep architecture for modeling multi-view metadata to predict mood scores with 90.31% accuracy on depression scores from session-level typing dynamics.

research.problem: Detecting mood disturbances and severity using mobile phone typing dynamics metadata.
research.motivation: Smartphones provide unobtrusive, real-time data for studying mental health in daily life settings.
research.objective: Evaluate feasibility of inferring mood states from typing dynamics and develop a multi-view fusion model.
research_questions: How do typing dynamics correlate with mood states in bipolar disorder?
Can multi-view metadata be effectively fused for mood prediction?

methodology.summary: DeepMood uses late fusion of GRU models for multi-view metadata (alphanumeric, special characters, accelerometer) with three fusion strategies: Multi-view Machines, Factorization Machines, and fully connected approaches.
methodology.training_strategy: End-to-end deep architecture with late fusion of multi-view time series

experiments.experimental_setup: Session-level analysis of 40 participants' typing data with HDRS/YMRS scores as ground truth.
experiments.results: 90.31% depression score prediction accuracy using session-level typing dynamics.

contributions: Data analysis of digital footprints in bipolar disorder
Two-stage late fusion framework for multi-view data
Empirical validation of mobile metadata for mood prediction
advantages: Handles unaligned and sparse multi-view time series
analysis.research_gap: Limited real-time data for affective symptom assessment

sections.introduction: Introduces smartphone data as a novel paradigm for mental health research and motivates mood detection through typing dynamics.
sections.methodology: Describes DeepMood's late fusion architecture and multi-view fusion strategies.
sections.results: Reports 90.31% depression prediction accuracy using session-level typing metadata.
sections.discussion: Analyzes correlations between typing dynamics and mood states across different views.
sections.conclusion: Demonstrates feasibility of using mobile metadata for mood disturbance detection with DeepMood.
